bullets.text: Q3 CR of 100.4 reflected stress in the system; YTD CR was 95.6, just under the 96 target; Personal Lines CR was 100.2, Commercial Lines CR was 89.5, and Property CR was 142.3.

Q3 recognized 6.4 points of catastrophe losses, including Hurricane Ida, the costliest storm in company history; Property estimated $450M incurred losses and ALAE from Ida, exceeding its $200M per-event retention.

YTD filed and elevated rate increases represented ~5% in personal auto; addressing regulatory scrutiny on rate increases; Property reducing volatile-state exposure via higher deductibles, rates, and targeted non-renewals.
Companywide NPW grew 13% in Q3 and 15% YTD; Commercial Lines NPW increased 47%, driven by trucking segment strength and economic factors; Property NPW rose 16%; Personal Lines NPW grew 7%.
Companywide PIF +9% YOY; personal auto crossed 17.5M milestone, adding nearly 1.3M PIFs LTM; Robinson PIFs grew low double digits, though new business applications dropped ~16% YOY.

Experiencing accelerating trends in average loss costs and sustained increases in loss frequency relative to Q3 2020; three large catastrophe events accounted for 24 points of YTD Property combined ratio.
Auto 8.7 model deployed across 17 states, representing ~40% countrywide premium; commercial auto 8.0 system active in 19 states (>50% premium); BOP expanded to 29 states (~55% market).

Total investment portfolio returned 0.2%; portfolio duration was reduced to 3.0 years from 3.1 years; share price volatility presented an opportunity to engage in share repurchases after a period of relative inactivity.
Slowed advertising spend to prioritize regaining auto product profitability over volume; appointed Remi Kent as Chief Marketing Officer, effective November 1, succeeding retiring CMO Jeff Charney.

Announced executive succession: John Murphy named Claims President succeeding retiring Mike Sieger; Lori Niederst transitioned from CHRO to CRM President; expanding claims and servicing staff to support Commercial Lines growth.
